rows.name: Qur'an
rows.detail: Explicit basis: 65:6 (pay the wages), 28:26-27 ('hire him — the best you can hire is the strong and trustworthy'), 18:77 (a wage for the wall). Root a-j-r.
rows.detail_long: Who: The Qur'an is the first rung of every USUL ladder: it is never dated, and every later rung refers back to it. What: Three separate revelations legitimize hire: the command to pay nursing wages (65:6), Shu'ayb's daughter urging Musa's hiring (28:26-27), and Khidr's remark that a wage could have been taken for rebuilding the wall (18:77). The verses, in the translation held in the Gold Ark Library: 28:26 — “One of the women said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy."” 28:27 — “He said, "Indeed, I wish to wed you one of these, my two daughters, on [the condition] that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it will be [as a favor] from you. And I do not wish to put you in difficulty. You will find me, if Allah wills, from among the righteous."” 18:77 — “So they set out, until when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. And they found therein a wall about to collapse, so al-Khidh r restored it. [Moses] said, "If you wished, you could have taken for it a payment."” Why here: The Qur'an opens the Ijarah ladder and is never dated. Source: Qur'an 65:6; 28:26; 28:27; 18:77.

rows.name: Sunan Ibn Majah 2443
rows.detail: 'Give the worker his wages before his sweat dries.'
rows.detail_long: Who: Sunan Ibn Majah was compiled by Ibn Majah al-Qazwini (824-887); it is the last of the six canonical Sunni hadith collections. Narrator: Abdullah bin Umar. What: The wage-promptness command, graded Sahih — the ethical core of every hire contract. The report, as held in the Gold Ark Library: “The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Give the worker his wages before his sweat dries.”” It stands in The Chapter on Pawning. Why here: 'Prophet's sayings (hadith)' rung of the Ijarah ladder; shown at 610 (no dated record; placed at the start of the Prophetic period (610)). Source: Sunan Ibn Majah 2443.

rows.name: Sahih Bukhari 2227
rows.detail: Hadith qudsi: Allah will oppose on the Day of Resurrection 'one who employs a laborer, takes full work, and does not pay his wages.'
rows.detail_long: Who: Sahih al-Bukhari was compiled by Imam al-Bukhari (810-870), the most celebrated hadith scholar in Sunni Islam; it is widely regarded as the most authentic collection after the Qur'an. Narrator: Abu Huraira. What: One of three persons Allah declares Himself against — the unpaid-labor prohibition that grounds the enforceability of wage claims. The report, as held in the Gold Ark Library: “The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Allah says, 'I will be against three persons on the Day of Resurrection: -1. One who makes a covenant in My Name, but he proves treacherous. -2. One who sells a free person (as a slave) and eats the price, -3. And one who employs a laborer and gets the full work done by him but does not pay him his wages.” It stands in Sales and Trade. Why here: 'Prophet's sayings (hadith)' rung of the Ijarah ladder; shown at 610 (no dated record; placed at the start of the Prophetic period (610)). Source: Sahih Bukhari 2227.

rows.name: Sahih Bukhari 2263
rows.detail: The Prophet and Abu Bakr hired a pagan expert guide from Bani al-Dil for the Hijra — dated to 622 CE, high confidence.
rows.detail_long: Who: Sahih al-Bukhari was compiled by Imam al-Bukhari (810-870), the most celebrated hadith scholar in Sunni Islam; it is widely regarded as the most authentic collection after the Qur'an. Narrator: Aisha. What: Aisha's narration: camels entrusted to the hired guide, rendezvous at the Cave of Thaur three days later. Hire across religious lines, on trust, at the community's most dangerous hour — and it is dated to the Hijra year itself. The report (opening), as held in the Gold Ark Library: “The Prophet (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr رضی اللہ عنہ employed a (pagan) man from the tribe of Bani Ad-Dail and the tribe of Bani 'Abu bin `Adi as a guide. He was an expert guide and he broke the oath contract which he had to abide by with the tribe of Al-`Asi bin Wail and he was on the religion of Quraish pagans. The Prophet (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr رضی اللہ عنہ had confidence in him and gave him their riding camels and told him to bring them to the Cave of Thaur after three days. [...]” It stands in Hiring. Why here: 'Prophet's sayings (hadith)' rung of the Ijarah ladder; shown at 622 (dated record in the Gold Ark Library). Source: Sahih Bukhari 2263.

rows.name: al-Tabari
rows.detail: Al-Tabari on 28:26 and 65:6 establishes hire/wage legitimacy and conditions.
rows.detail_long: Who: Abu Ja'far al-Tabari (839-923) was a Sunni scholar, historian, jurist and Qur'an commentator from Amol in Tabaristan who worked in Baghdad. He followed the Shafi'i school for nearly a decade, then developed his own school of law (the Jariri school), which lasted about two centuries after him. He is best known for his Qur'an commentary, Tafsir al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan), and his historical chronicle. What: Al-Tabari on 28:26 and 65:6 validates wage labor from both directions: Shu'ayb's daughter's 'hire him — the strong, the trustworthy' as the employer's criteria, and the command to pay nursing mothers their wages as the duty side. Why here: 'Qur'an commentary (tafsir)' rung of the Ijarah ladder; shown at 923 (year of the author's death). Source: Jami' al-Bayan (Tafsir al-Tabari), on Q28:26.

rows.name: Fakhr al-Din Razi
rows.detail: Al-Razi's commentary adds the conditions analysis of hire.
rows.detail_long: Who: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi (1149-1209) was a theologian and polymath, known as the 'Sultan of the Theologians'. His Qur'an commentary, Tafsir al-Kabir (Mafatih al-Ghayb), is described as the most varied and many-sided of its kind. What: Tafsir al-Kabir dissects what makes a hire valid — known work, known wage, capable worker — the analytic layer between scripture and fiqh manuals. Why here: 'Qur'an commentary (tafsir)' rung of the Ijarah ladder, Shafi'i voice; shown at 1209 (year of the author's death). Source: Mafatih al-Ghayb (Tafsir al-Kabir).

rows.name: Ibn Abbas (attrib., Tanwir al-Miqbas)
rows.detail: The earliest attributed gloss on 28:26 — 'Hire him! the best you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.'
rows.detail_long: Who: Abd Allah ibn Abbas (618-686) was a cousin of the Prophet Muhammad, remembered as the 'Scholar of the Umma' and highly regarded for his knowledge of traditions and his interpretation of the Qur'an. The commentary Tanwir al-Miqbas is attributed to him by tradition; the attribution is traditional, not critical, which is why the work is marked 'attrib.' What: Tanwir al-Miqbas on the Moses hiring verse: the strong 'who can bear a heavy load', the trustworthy 'regarding that with which you entrust him'. The Qur'an's own two-line job specification — competence plus integrity — glossed at the very start of the tafsir tradition. Attribution traditional, not critical — hence 'attrib.' Why here: 'Qur'an commentary (tafsir)' rung of the Ijarah ladder; shown at 687 (death of Ibn Abbas, to whom the work is attributed). Source: Tanwir al-Miqbas (attrib. Ibn Abbas), on Q28:26.

rows.name: Mufti Muhammad Shafi Usmani
rows.detail: Ma'ariful Qur'an on 28:26: the two qualities every hire requires — strength for the work, trustworthiness with what is entrusted.
rows.detail_long: Who: Mufti Muhammad Shafi Usmani (1897-1976) was born in Deoband, became chief mufti of Darul Uloom Deoband in 1931, and later Grand Mufti of Pakistan in Karachi. His best-known work, Ma'ariful Qur'an, is an Urdu commentary on the whole Qur'an that began as a decade of weekly radio lectures. He belonged to the Hanafi school and the Deobandi movement. What: Ma'ariful Qur'an on 28:26: Shu'ayb's daughter argues the case for hiring Moses on exactly two grounds — 'he should be strong, and... he should be trustworthy'. The modern mufassir drawing the employment doctrine straight from the verse: capability plus amanah as the hiring test. Why here: 'Qur'an commentary (tafsir)' rung of the Ijarah ladder, Hanafi voice; shown at 1976 (year of the author's death). Source: Ma'ariful Qur'an, on Q28:26.

rows.name: Ibn Rushd
rows.detail: Comparative validation: all four schools accept ijarah by Qur'an, Sunnah and consensus; only Ibn al-Asamm rejected it.
rows.detail_long: Who: Ibn Rushd (1126-1198), known in the West as Averroes, was an Andalusian polymath and jurist of Cordoba who trained in Maliki law and served as a judge. He wrote Bidayat al-Mujtahid on the differences between the schools of law and the principles behind them; his biographer Ibn al-Abbar called him especially competent in the study of juristic disagreement. What: Bidayat records near-unanimity on leasing — the lone dissent (Ibn al-Asamm, on uncertainty grounds) proving the rule. In the work itself (vol. and page 4:5; our literal translation from the Arabic): “Hire (ijara) is permissible according to all the jurists of the garrison-cities [regions], and the first generation. And its prohibition was reported from al-Asamm and Ibn 'Ulayya.” It also states: “And the proof of the majority is His saying, exalted is He: {I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine} [al-Qasas: 27], the verse; and His saying: {then if they suckle for you, give them their wages} [al-Talaq: 6].” It also states: “And the hadith of Jabir: "that he sold a camel to the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - and stipulated its back [i.e. riding it] as far as Madina." And what may be taken in full by stipulation may be taken in full by wage.” It also states: “[The doubt of those who forbade it:] and the usufructs in hires are non-existent at the time of the contract, so that was gharar (uncertainty) and of [the kind of] selling what has not been created.” Why here: 'Classical law schools' rung of the Ijarah ladder, Maliki voice; shown at 1198 (year of the author's death). Source: Bidayat al-Mujtahid.

rows.name: Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi
rows.detail: Al-Mughni vol. VI: the detailed Hanbali rulebook of leasing; Malikis/Hanbalis add the 'lawful benefits' limit.
rows.detail_long: Who: Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi (1147-1223) was a jurist of the Hanbali school who studied in Baghdad and taught in Damascus; he is regarded as one of the school's most authoritative classical figures. He is best known for al-Mughni, a legal encyclopedia that compares the opinions of the Sunni schools while setting out the Hanbali position in detail. He also wrote 'Umdat al-Fiqh. What: The leasing book of al-Mughni covers usufruct definition, rent conditions and termination — with the Maliki-Hanbali restriction that only lawful benefits can be leased. In the work itself (vol. and page 5:321; our literal translation from the Arabic): “The basis for the permissibility of hire (ijara) is the Book and the Sunna, and consensus. As for the Book, it is the saying of God, exalted is He: {then if they suckle for you, give them their wages} [al-Talaq: 6].” It also states: “And as for the Sunna, it is established "that the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - and Abu Bakr hired a man from Banu al-Dil as a skilled guide."” It also states: “[From the hadith the page cites from al-Bukhari, from Abu Hurayra, "three whose opponent I am on the Day of Resurrection":] and a man who hired a hireling and took in full from him and did not pay him his wage in full.” It also states: “And the people of knowledge in every age and every city agreed on the permissibility of hire, except what is reported from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asamm, that he said: that is not permissible; because it is gharar (uncertainty).” Why here: 'Classical law schools' rung of the Ijarah ladder, Hanbali voice; shown at 1223 (year of the author's death). Source: Al-Mughni, vol. VI.

rows.name: AAOIFI
rows.detail: AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 9: ijarah + lease-ending-in-ownership (IMB) — engine of asset finance and ijarah sukuk.
rows.detail_long: Who: AAOIFI (the Accounting and Auditing Organization for Islamic Financial Institutions) issues the Shari'ah Standards. They are mandatory in Bahrain, its home jurisdiction, and adopted in the UAE and other countries. What: SS9 codifies operating and financing leases plus ijarah muntahia bittamleek. Rules adopted 31 May 2000, reformatted as Standard 16 May 2002. Clauses read in the standard's text: 3/1 the lease must be preceded by acquisition of the asset or its usufruct; 4/1/1 the lease is binding on both parties; 4/1/2 duration must be specified; 5/1/1 the leased asset must be usable while preserved and the benefit Shari'ah-permissible; 7/1/1 sale of the asset to the lessee terminates the ijarah; 8/1 in Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek the title transfer must sit in a document SEPARATE from the lease. Why here: 'Modern rules & standards' rung of the Ijarah ladder; shown at 2002 (adopted as rules 29-31 May 2000 (meeting 4); readopted as a Standard at meeting 8, 11-16 May 2002). Source: AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 9.
